purpose: manual and automated end-to-end validation of the accepted single-server multiplayer architecture through the ordinary controller, Seven Days inventory UI and physical 3D item interactions
acceptance: two ordinary graphical Godot clients use the same dedicated authority
clients submit InputMap movement intent while the server computes canonical position velocity and interaction origin
client-authored PLAYER_STATE position velocity basis and interaction position are rejected
pickup uses authoritative player range and deterministic server visibility checks
drop and placement transforms are constructed and bounded by the server
both clients use the existing seven_days_like presentation profile with ten hotbar slots
M7 durable state with a ten-slot hotbar survives stop or kill, server restart, reconnect and continued gameplay
server and both clients converge on player and Item Graph checksums while connected
disconnect and shutdown leave no Godot process or resource leak
M3 and M5 acceptance compositions remain available
out_of_scope: client-side movement prediction rollback and lag compensation
physics-engine collision simulation for the dedicated movement integrator beyond the bounded playground controller
production content and final level design
